name: setns-nonruntime
why: setns from a non-runtime process is the container-escape namespace-join primitive
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for setns_namespace_join_behavioral.c's setns() record

name: setns-shell-escape
why: a shell in a compromised container joining a host namespace fd is the same escape from a different, non-runtime process
source: synthetic: an interactive shell calling setns toward a host namespace

name: lsns-nsget-ioctl-no-setns
why: lsns inspects namespaces with ioctl(ns_fd, NS_GET_*) but joins none; it keeps the SYSCALL surface on a namespace fd but is not setns, so the setns syscall anchor must be load-bearing. openat/ioctl of /proc/<pid>/ns/* is NOT the audited step (atomic.rules records setns, not openat), so this models the audited ioctl lsns really makes instead
source: recorded: strace of lsns on this host -- ioctl(fd, NS_GET_USERNS 0xb701); only ioctl (not openat) is in detections/audit/atomic.rules

name: unshare-new-namespace
why: unshare creates a NEW namespace rather than joining an existing one, so it is not the escape primitive; flipping only the syscall name to setns fires
source: synthetic: unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) by a non-runtime process

name: runc-rootfs-setns-allowlisted
why: runc's main process enters the new container's mount namespace during `runc run` (setns(ns_fd, CLONE_NEWNS)); this is the one setns path that runs as comm 'runc', which the allowlist suppresses. The high-volume container-exec path (docker/kubectl exec) runs as comm 'runc:[1:CHILD]'/'runc:[2:INIT]', which the 'runc' allowlist does NOT match and so fires -- a rule defect tracked in detections/RULE_DEFECTS.md L1
source: recorded: strace of `runc run` (runc 1.5.1) on this host -- comm 'runc' setns(18, CLONE_NEWNS=0x20000) during rootfs setup

name: nsenter-allowlisted
why: nsenter is an allowlisted admin tool that joins namespaces by design; the allowlist must filter it
source: recorded: strace of util-linux/busybox nsenter joining a container's namespaces -- comm 'nsenter' setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS=0x20000)
